The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- for the grievous injuries sustained by him, in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 07.07.2021 at about 06.30 pm., the petitioner was riding Bajaj Discovery motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-J-6879 slowly and cautiously by following traffic rules on the left side of the road on NH-48, Bangalore - Tumkur SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.4427/2021 Service Road, Near Rauthanahalli cross,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, Bangalore District.

At that time, the driver of the Maruthi Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MV-0574 driven by its driver with high speed endangering human life and property and without giving any signal suddenly turn at the Rauthnahalli cross road and dashed back side of car and caused the accident.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
he was taken to V.P.Magnus Hospital, Nelamangala after first aid he was taken to Sanjayagandhi Hospital, Bangalore and took treatement as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent huge amount towards his treatment, medicines and other expenses.

3. Further the petitioner has stated that, at the time of accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 37 years and working as a Coolie and also agriculturist and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he is not able to do his work.

Further he has stated that in relation to SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.4427/2021 accident, FIR came to be registered in Cr.No.235/2021 at Nelamangala Traffic Police station against the driver of Maruthi Car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
Hence, he has prayed to award compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- from the respondents.
4. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and hence, he has been placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through his counsel and filed the objections to main petition.

Prathap vs Rentease International Llp on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17029665/
2
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.
Respondent No.1 denied the age, income and treatment taken by the petitioner.
Further contended that, the petitioner did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the motor cycle involved in the accident and he is responsible for the alleged accident.

Respondent No.2 denied the involvement of the Maruthi Car in the accident and the Respondent No.1 being the SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.4427/2021 owner of the Maruthi Car has colluded with the petitioner and has not intimated about the accident to the Respondent No.2.
Hence, there is gross violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has admitted that he issued policy with respect to Maruthi Car bearing reg.No.KA-04-MV-0574 as such, his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has further contended that if this Tribunal pleases to award then the rate of interest may be restricted 6% per annum.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues arise for my consideration:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 07.07.2021 at about 6.30 pm., he was proceeding on a bike bearing No.KA-06-J-6879 on NH-48, Bengaluru-Tumkur service road, near Ravuthanahalli cross, at that time, car bearing No.KA-04-MV-0574 being driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner took the turn without giving signals as such he dashed at the rear portion of the car and due to impact he fell on the ground and sustained grievous SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.4427/2021 injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
6 . The petitioner in order to prove his case he has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
He has examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P.18 to Ex.P.20.
7. The Respondent No.2 - insurance company has not adduced rebuttal evidence.
8. Heard the argument of learned counsel for the Petitioner.
Perused the entire records.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

3  REASONS 10.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:
In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.
He has got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.17.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination- in-chief.
11. The petitioner in order to substantiate his case has got examined himself as PW.1.

He has filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and has re- iterated the averments made in the petition and has produced FIR, complaint, wound certificate,
spot panchanama, rough sketch, IMV report and charge sheet marked as Ex.P.1 to P.5, P.8 and 9 by these oral and documentary evidence Petitioner proved that, there was an accident in which he sustained injury.

12. On perusal of complaint Ex.P.2 which reveals that owner of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-J-6879 has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the complaint, Nelamangala police have registered FIR SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.4427/2021 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. With regard to negligence, Respondent No.2- insurance Company has mainly contended that it was the negligence of the Petitioner himself, but no documents have been produced.

It is contended by the insurance company that the driver of insured vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the car which is involved in the alleged accident and owner of the car entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid and effective driving licence and caused the accident.
Further contended that, rider of alleged motor cycle was not wearing helmet and without having driving licence and due to his negligence accident occurred.

Except this suggestion,
Respondent - Insurance Company has not produced any material to show the negligence of the Petitioner as well as driver of the Maruthi car.
The complaint has been filed on the next day of accident and the negligence of the offending vehicle is alleged.
Neither the owner nor the driver of the offending Maruthi Car SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.4427/2021 has challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending Maruthi Car.
The I.O. has filed charge sheet after complete investigation based on the evidences available at the spot.
14. All the records indicate the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent-insurance Company has also failed to prove the negligence of Petitioner in the accident.
By the above materials and evidences it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in RTA due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
The Petitioner states that he was aged about 37 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to V.P.Magnus Hospital, Nelamangala after first aid he was taken to NIMHANS and Sanjayagandhi Hospital,
Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

As per Ex.P.11 - discharge summary petitioner took SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.4427/2021 treatment from 08.07.2021 to Prathap vs Rentease International Llp on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17029665/
4 20.07.2021 i.e., for a period of 13 days.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a Coolie and also Agriculturist and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he has not resumed to his normal work, not in a position to do his work as he was doing prior to the accident and lost his present and future earnings.

Dr.Chidanand.K.J.C, Orthopedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained right both bone leg fracture type 1 and patient underwent external fixator on 17.07.2021 and later discharged on 20.07.2021.

Further, PW.2 has stated that on 16.01.2023 patient came for disability assessment and noted healed surgical scar mark over right ankle, mild swelling of right leg, ankle, thickening of bones right leg felt, range of movements of right knee and ankle restricted, daily activities cross leg sitting, squatting for using Indian toilets were found to be difficulty and SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.4427/2021 X-ray shows fracture mal-united.
On examination PW.2 has assessed permanent physical disability for right lower limb at 48% and to the whole body at 16%.

Along with his evidence, PW.2 has produced OPD slip, entire case sheet and X-ray at Ex.P.18 to 20.
17.

Therefore by considering the evidence on record and doctor opinion, I am of the opinion that, the disability of the petitioner has to be taking into consideration for his physical disability to award compensation.

So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following different heads:
18. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON THE ACCOUNT OF DISABILITY.

According to the petitioner he doing coolie and was an agriculturist and he was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
To support of his claim with respect to avocation and earnings, he has not produced any documents.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.

entities.text: Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 13.01.2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
20. The Petitioner in support of his age he has produced Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10.

As per Ex.P.10 he was born in the year 1989 and he was aged about 32 years as on alleged accident.
Therefore, the proper multiplier applicable to be the case on hand is 16.
21.
The Petitioner claims that due to injury sustained in the accident, he was not in a position to stand for a long time, lift weight, climb stair case, walk fast and got sever affect to his profession.

As Prathap vs Rentease International Llp on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17029665/
5 stated supra he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month by doing SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.4427/2021 coolie work and was an agriculturist.
The PW.2 has assessed the permanent physical disability to right lower limb at 48% and 16% disability to the whole body.

During cross examination PW.2 has deposed that, fractures are mal-united, he can do agriculture work with some difficulty, since the petitioner is aged 35 years there is a chance of recovery in future, the restrictions are mild to moderate, there is no shortening of bone and there is no loss of muscle power.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, it is proper to take 10% disability to the whole body.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,88,000/- (Rs.15,000/- X 12 X 16 X 10/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.

22. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and was inpatient for a period of 13 days which caused him to SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.4427/2021 immeasurable mental agony and pain.
Hence, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/- would be just and proper compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
23. LOSS OF AMENITIES
Further on perusal of evidence of PW.1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained injury and the same is mentioned above paras.
The petitioner was aged about 32 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of PW.1 and PW.2,
considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
24. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Ex.P.11 - Discharge summary shows that the Petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital from 08.07.2021 to 20.07.2021 i.e. for a period of 13 days.

Therefore, it is just and SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.4427/2021 reasonable to award compensation of Rs.13,000/- under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.

25. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD AND REST PERIOD:- With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, considering 13 days admitted in the hospital as inpatient and around 2 month for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as Rs.15,000/- per month, Petitioner is awarded Rs.45,000/- towards loss of earning during laid up period.

26. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on 10 medical bills at Ex.P.12.

On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent Rs.15,080/- towards medical Prathap vs Rentease International Llp on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17029665/
6 expenses.
The medical bills appear to be genuine in the absence of challenge.
Therefore, the Petitioner is SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.4427/2021 entitled for medical expenses of Rs.15,080/- towards Medical Expenses.
27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
During cross examination PW.2 deposed that, he has not suggested any future surgery, implants are removed.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of Future medical expenses.

28. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reasons, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,06,080/- under the following heads:

1. Loss of future earning Rs. 2,88,000/-
capacity due to permanent disability 2. Towards Pain and Sufferings Rs. 25,000/-
3. Towards loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000/-

4 . Towards attendant, food Rs. 13,000/-
and nourishment and conveyance charges 5. Towards loss of income Rs. 45,000/-
 SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.4427/2021  during laid up period and  rest period.
 6. Towards medical expenses Rs. 15,080/-

Towards future medical ---  Expenses  TOTAL Rs. 4,06,080/-
29. Regarding Interest & Liability: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

29. Regarding Interest & Liability: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

Respondent No.1 being the insured of the offending vehicle, the Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation with interest at 6% p.a. to the Petitioner as issuance of policy and subsistence of policy is not disputed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative.

: in view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;

The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,06,080/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Six Thousand and Eighty only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
